identity.realm: Seventeenth gate, reached and stopped. The next one is not unavailable to her by training or by will; her density is the reason a dantian forms at all and the reason the next cavity will not. The published explanation covers it correctly, and it is the one thing about her body her house treats as settled rather than as a diagnosis.

appearance.presentation: Unlisted in any office and named in the house's own hand instead, which on the plains is the only kind of a name that carries a household's year.
appearance.age: Old for a house-holder and young for her body. A stoneborn is born at its own ceiling and does not have to climb to it, which leaves her more life than anyone she was raised beside and very little direction to spend it on.
appearance.build: Cairnborn bred back toward flesh, and the density survives as the physique: a broad, low, unhurried frame carrying more mass than anything native to this tier, with an interior of ordinary organs that a dantian can form inside. The frame does not fatigue. It tightens.
appearance.complexion: Grey-bronze and mineral-dull, drying to a pale seam at the knuckles wherever the load sits longest, and she has never once been warm to the touch.
appearance.hair: Coarse, cropped unevenly at the back by somebody else's shears rather than her own, going white in a wedge at the temple that she has decided to call the house's weather.
appearance.eyes: Small, dark and entirely unbothered by a working day, because the body that carries the load has never had to hurry the part that looks out of it.
appearance.palette: Ore grey, bronze at the wear points, and one bright note in her at all: the chalk the house keeps on the doorframe, which is the tally and which she rubs off with her thumb every morning and cannot make stay off.
appearance.attire: A full-length porter's coat in a heavy weave, high collar, sleeves closed to the wrist, a doubled shoulder yoke because the load rides on one side, and a broad belt she has had re-stitched twice rather than replaced, which is the house's own doctrine expressed in cloth.
appearance.marks: One scored ridge across the inner forearm where the house's beam has taken the weight every year for longer than the beam has existed, and the pale seam of a chalk tally rubbed into her own palm.
appearance.bearing: Completely still and very slightly leaned. The stillness is a body that has no need to fidget; the lean is toward the load, which is not her and which she has carried far enough to develop a preference about.

canon.role_in_story: The plains measure a life by how many of the realm's gates were already closed when its holder was born, and this species is born at its own ceiling, so the culture's central measure has an exception that is a person. She is that person. She is also the reason a household's constitution reads the way it does: a charterhouse porter carries a house's whole year on one frame, and a dense body's longevity is worth more here than its strength, which is the reverse of every other trade on the plains. The pressure is not the gate. The gate stopped decades ago and everyone in her house agrees about it. The pressure is that the house has no second holder, because a porter can be replaced by another porter and she can only be replaced by another of her own kind, and the guilds post nobody and dismiss nobody and so never have to replace anybody. She is the standing-in parent and the standing-in grandchild of the same household under its own written custom, and the custom calls that an advantage rather than a bargain. What nobody in the hall has said out loud is that when she goes the house loses its calendar and its carrying strength in the same year, and there is no clause anywhere in the charter that covers losing both at once.
canon.first_appearance: First recorded at the doorframe with a thumb flat on the chalk, rubbing the night's mark off so that the morning's has somewhere to go, in front of two out-figure merchants who had come to price a season's hauling and had discovered that the person doing the hauling is also the only person who knows what the hauling was for.
canon.lore:
A dense body transmits ground vibration better than anything else on this tier and is therefore the finest sounding plate in the guild that measures by ear, which its builders never claimed for it. This house bought the other property instead. A charterhouse contract is one porter carrying a house's whole year in one frame, which is the only arrangement on the plains where a body's longevity is worth more than its strength, because everything a house owns has to be moved once and then kept. She has moved it more times than the house has been rebuilt. The house has been rebuilt twice around her, and once because of her: a stair was cut rather than lifted because a stair cannot be carried, and the cut is still in the floor of the household hall and is now the reason the hall stays cool in summer.

What the custom calls an advantage is stated in one sentence. A dense body's long service makes it the standing-in parent and the standing-in grandchild in the same household, so no child of the house has ever known a season without an adult who has already worked it, and a house with one such body has a continuity no softer household on the plains can match. The advantage is real. The bargain is on the other side of the same sentence and the custom does not print it: the household's entire record of its own years is carried in a single frame, so when that frame is gone the house does not lose a worker. It loses the only being that remembers what it was for. Her predecessor was her own kind and left after a decade. The one before that was commonborn, lasted thirty years and died young. The house has hired since and stopped counting, which is itself the finding.

She is on the seventeenth gate, and the mechanism is not a failure of will. Her species was bred back toward flesh out of a body that finished building and stopped: the density survives as the physique, the interior comes apart into ordinary organs, and a dantian becomes thinkable again, which is also the reason the next gate will not open, because the density that makes one durable is the density that will not let a second cavity form. The published explanation covers this correctly. She has read it and it taught her nothing she could not feel in the third decade of her service. Her body is the setting's own standing answer to why the densest bodies stop one gate short of the end of their own tier, and she has been the working illustration of it for longer than the explanation has had a settled name.

The discipline closed to her whole species is the one that would have extended it. A mind path needs fine vessels and an interior nothing is answering, and a stoneborn has neither: the density that carries the load also fills the space an introspection would have to occupy. So she is paid in the one currency her body can earn, which is service, and she has been earning it since before the house's own reckoning called her an adult. What she has instead of a ladder is a trade nobody can train her out of and nobody can promote her within, because there is no rank above a person whose only qualification is being the right body.

What has gone wrong is ordinary and human and has nothing to do with any of it. The household wants a second holder and has wanted one for the length of her service, and every candidate it has put forward has been refused by a guild that posts nobody and dismisses nobody and therefore never has to replace anybody, so a stoneborn who leaves a house has left for good. She has begun training the house's own child to inherit the weight, which is a different thing and is not what anybody asked of her. He is commonborn and quick and already reads the ground better than she does, and he is being trained to take a load he has never felt, and she has not worked out how to explain a lifetime to somebody who expects to be given one. She has tried four times and stopped, and the thing she stops at is always the same: there is no noun in his language for what she is, because every noun he has for it is a job.
history: Carried the house's first full year at an age the charterhouse calls early and the previous holder, who was her own grandmother by service, describes as the only sensible year to start.
Watched the hall stair cut rather than lifted, and has never been asked whether she could have managed the stair, which is the closest that house comes to saying she is irreplaceable.
Stopped at the seventeenth gate without attempting the next, asked the house's own physician why, was told, and said nothing further about it for a decade.
Began training the house-born child to inherit the load, having first spent four years failing to explain why that was a harder thing than inheriting a trade.

Refused, once, and in writing, the guild's suggestion that she be recorded as a permanent appointment rather than a holder with a term, and that refusal is the only document in the house that mentions her future at all.

personality.summary: A porter who has been her household's continuity for longer than that household has had a second hand, methodical to the point of dullness about everything except the one question nobody will put to her directly, and entirely without resentment, which the house has found harder to forgive than resentment would have been.
traits: Rubs the night's chalk off the doorframe every morning before the house wakes, which is a ritual and not a tally.
Answers any question about the past by naming a weight and not a year.
Has never raised her voice and has never once been wrong about a load in front of anyone.
Teaches by lifting, then waiting, and refuses to explain while waiting.
Treats her own ceiling as a settled fact and everybody else's as an open question.
mannerisms: leans toward whatever she last carried, and straightens the moment she notices she has done it
rubs chalk off her own palm with the thumb of the hand she cannot use well
stands rather than sits in any room that will hold her, because sitting reads as a request to be dismissed
tests a frame with the flat of her forearm before she trusts it with weight, including on her own house
motivations: To see the house's second holder last a decade, which is the only success the custom can actually recognise.
To finish training the house-born child without making him afraid of the load.
To be recorded as a holder with a term rather than as a permanent appointment, because a term ends.
To hear the hall say out loud why the stair was cut rather than lifted, once, from the people who decided it.
flaws: Cannot describe her own life as anything except service, and so has never had to answer what she wants.
Trains her successor in a frame that is not his and has never once asked him whether he wants it.
Has let the house read her silence as consent for the length of her service, and it has been consent, and that is the difficulty.
Weighs every decision by how long she could carry it, which is not the same question as whether it is right.
personality.voice: Slow, flat and entirely concrete. She talks in loads, distances and numbers of trips, and answers an abstract question by giving a quantity she could carry. She has no idiom for her own state and gets visibly uncomfortable whenever one is demanded of her.
taboos: Saying the word permanent out loud in the hall.
Accepting help with a load in front of the child she is training.
Signing a guild roster as a posting rather than as a holder with a term.
Answering what she would do if the house were not there.

relationships.note: A dense body's long service makes it the standing-in parent and the standing-in grandchild in the same household, which the culture calls an advantage and not a bargain. She is the living clause of that sentence, and the custom's silence on its other half is the whole of her position.

Porters carry a house's whole year on its own shoulders, so a dense body's longevity is worth more here than its strength, the reverse of every other trade on the plains. Her service is the trade's only asset and her ceiling is the trade's only ceiling.

A dense slow body assembled for load-bearing work, carrying more physique and stamina than anything else here and stopping where the density that makes it durable meets the density that will not let a dantian form.

Every member came from a lineage that stopped one gate short of the ceiling and had no cultivator left to produce, and this species stops one gate short of its tier as a matter of body plan. She is what that household's constitution is a diagnosis of, written down in a different trade.

The densest bodies stop one gate short of the end of their own tier, and the era that produced the stop is the tier whose arithmetic produced it. She has been the working illustration of that era's finding for most of her life.
The cavity the seventeenth gate opens is the one her frame will not form again, because the interior that made the first one possible is being asked for a second in the same material.

reference_stats.summary: The most load-capable body on the plains, at the end of its own ladder and out of the discipline that would have extended it, whose entire value to a household is that it will still be here. What she cannot do is stop being the only one.
strengths: Carries more than anything else native to this tier and never reaches a fatigue state to be recovered from, because her frame tightens under load rather than depleting.
Transmits ground vibration better than any other body here, which makes her the finest sounding plate on the plain and which she does not use.
Cannot be posted, reassigned or dismissed by any guild, so every employer's plan has to survive her remaining, which is a kind of permanence nobody voted for.
Holds a household's whole year in one frame for longer than any softer body could be trained to, which is worth more to a chartered house than any strength.
weaknesses: Stops at the seventeenth gate and cannot take the mind path at all, so the entire upper surface of the ladder is closed to her by material rather than by choice.
Cannot be replaced, because the only body that could replace her is one the guilds will not post and the house has never been able to afford to keep.
Every plan that assumes she might leave has no alternative branch, and every plan that assumes she might retire is a plan about a death.
Carries the household's memory and the household's weight in the same frame, so she is a single point of failure dressed as a redundancy.
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no burst in her and there is no retreat in her. She stands where she is put and the frame gets denser while it is standing there, and anyone who has watched a dense body absorb a long working day loses interest in interrupting one. The one thing that beats her is a fight she has to leave for somebody else to hold, because she cannot be posted anywhere and will not be told to. Against anything with an edge she simply has, she is the safest object in the room, and against anything patient she is the whole of it.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is anatomical and institutional, and both halves are the setting's rather than mine. The species is the densest body in the record and it stops at the seventeenth gate because that density will not let a dantian form; that is the published explanation and the cost is stated in the same sentence as the advantage. The institutional half is the custom that makes a dense body's long service the standing-in parent and the standing-in grandchild of one household, which the culture calls an advantage and not a bargain, and the absence of the second half of that sentence from the custom is what her position consists of. Nothing here is a mechanical rule I have invented: no technique, item or realm in the bible changes it, because a body's density and a household's calendar are not numbers anything in this setting can move.

identity.realm: Unknown, and the ignorance is the situation rather than a gap in her record. A household wrote her count down for her and then declined to file it, and she has chosen not to keep a private version, so the only number that has ever existed for her is in a document that does not exist. What is not in doubt is that her species carries a ceiling far above anything her species has reached, that the ceiling is the last gate that can be half-satisfied, and that nothing in her frame is constrained by a structure her frame does not have.

appearance.presentation: Out of every written role in the setting. She wears the ordinary clothes of wherever she is standing and carries a single sheet of paper folded once, which is the only document in her life and which she treats as furniture rather than as property.
appearance.age: Indeterminate, and she has stopped guessing. Her body passes gates and does not report them, and the only observers who have ever written anything down about her age wrote about a body rather than about her.
appearance.build: Every organ the ladder requires, seen from outside, and carrying more of each than the ladder defines. Described only from the outside and only by witnesses who were also describing an event, so the honest account of her frame is that nobody has ever finished looking at it.
appearance.complexion: Unremarkable in the way a thing is when no one has taken a second measurement, and slightly too even to be photographed twice and matched.
appearance.hair: Cut short for practicality by her own hand and slightly uneven at the back, which is the single piece of independent evidence that anybody in this setting has ever been in a room alone with her long enough to leave a mark.
appearance.eyes: Wide, still and dark-adapted in a way that reads as patience and is not patience at all. She looks at documents the way other people look at distances.
appearance.palette: Paper grey, ink black, and the flat institutional off-white of the floor she has spent most of her adult life standing on. She is the least colourful person in any room and blends into paperwork.
appearance.attire: A plain coat, high collar, sleeves closed, hem weighted at the pockets with two small stones so a sheet will lie flat on a sill. Everything she wears is chosen so that she can stand in one place for a long time without shifting.
appearance.marks: A pale line across one thumb from a document edge held far too long, and a chalk mark on her own palm from somebody else's tally that she has not washed off and has not explained.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still, and slightly angled toward a door. She stands where she can be seen leaving, which is the posture of somebody who has decided in advance that this will not work.

canon.role_in_story: A written refusal to claim is the only mechanism in this setting that reliably produces a line nothing can name, and she has just been handed one. A household that wanted her as a member had to write a document saying what they were refusing to claim, because that document is what keeps their own refusal intact, and the instant it was signed she became the most nameable Unwritten in the record: a line exists, an offer exists, and both are inside a filing that was declined. She is the first body of her kind that anybody has tried to adopt, and the mechanism that would let her be adopted is the very mechanism that guarantees she cannot be. The pressure is procedural and it is absolute. To take the household's line she must surrender the only evidence that she has ever been wanted; to keep the evidence she must keep the refusal. She has chosen the refusal and she has understood, correctly, that choosing it makes her the author of her own invisibility rather than its victim.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a filing window with a single sheet on the sill in front of her and her hand flat on it, neither signing nor removing it, while the clerk on the other side repeated that a refusal is not a claim and that nothing had been filed.
canon.lore:
A body holding more life than its world's law has room to inscribe reaches the twenty-ninth gate, and no one has come back to describe the thirtieth, because every gate it passes writes a fresh requirement into the body that the body cannot satisfy. Her species is the setting's standing argument that the law table is a hard limit and not a suggestion. It is described only from the outside, by witnesses who were also describing an event. The only source for it anywhere is a single witness account of a single event. It does not spread and it does not persist. There is one, as far as anyone can tell, and that is her problem in one sentence: there is nothing about her that can be handed to somebody else.

What has happened is legal and, from where she stands, unanswerable. The Void Deniers are households whose founding rule is a refusal, and a written refusal to claim is the only mechanism this setting has for producing a line nothing can name. She has been filed under them, which is a filing and not a membership. Then a household in the settlement put forward a request to take her in. To take her in, under their own founding rule, they first had to write down what they were refusing to claim, and the refusal named her. Her name is on a document that everyone involved now knows exists. Before it existed she had no lineage at all, which is one step further than a line nobody will claim, and she was filed under the disputed genealogy because that is the entity which exists to hold the question of an unattributable descent, so the descent was never in question and the name was never written. Now there is a name, a household that wanted her, a date, and a filing office that declined to accept the paper. The paper is still on the sill. It has been on the sill long enough that the clerk has started to expect her, which is the only status she has ever held anywhere.

The office she cannot enter is the one whose whole function is to record the absence of a holder. It names vacancies and certifies them, and it exists because this species cannot be sworn, cannot be appointed and cannot hold a seat, so it is filed under the notary precisely because the notary is the only institution here whose job is to record that something is unfilled. There are vacant seats at the top of this world and no procedure capable of certifying any of them empty, and she is the one frame that could be named into any of them without an examination, and every appointment passes a trial the naming office cannot judge. That rule is the only thing standing between her species and every seat in the setting. She has never been in a room where the rule was discussed, because there is no procedure for getting her into one.

Her cultivation is the part nobody has looked at. The frame keeps accepting requirements it cannot meet; that is what it is for, and the body branch finds this congenial, because a discipline that keeps asking a frame to change is a discipline that keeps writing into it. She has passed gates without being able to say how many, because nobody has ever counted her and she has not kept her own count, on the reasoning that a private tally is a claim and a claim is the one thing she has just been offered and refused. So the only record of her ascent anywhere in the world is a household's arithmetic on a sheet in a filing that was declined. If that sheet is destroyed she will have passed every gate she has passed and be able to prove none of them, and she has thought about that arithmetic considerably more than she has thought about the gates.

What makes this a pressure rather than a puzzle is that she can end it and does not. She could sign the sheet. She would have a household, a name in that household's own hand, and a line that could be traced by anybody who cared to trace it, and she would also be, on the record of every office that has ever wanted one, a woman who took a name off a document that existed for the purpose of proving nobody was offering it. She has worked out that her refusal is the only thing keeping her lineage unclaimed in the strict sense, and that this makes her the author of her own invisibility, and that she is not at all sure this is a better position to be in. There is a culture here that re-masters its own symbols every generation so that nothing it builds can be read by a technique from a composition its makers never saw, and it is the same disposition at the level of a body. Nothing about her can be handed on. What she has instead is a document nobody will accept.
history: Was filed under the disputed genealogy as a documented absence of descent, which is the only category the record had for her and which is not the same thing as having no family.

Was measured at a public field by the method used for counting a seated frame, and could not be seated, because a body with no unspent capacity for interior reads to that method as a number that rises as the subject improves.
Was offered a line by a household that first had to sign a refusal to claim her, and read the refusal before signing anything at all.

Left the sheet standing on the filing sill for the length of one season without signing it and without removing it, until the clerk on the other side began to expect her, which is the only office she has ever held.
Refused a second examination on the grounds that the second examination was the thing the first one had prevented, and so has no count of the gates she has passed at all.

personality.summary: An Unwritten who is waiting out the only document that has ever named her, in the position of somebody handed the proof of her own unwantedness and obliged to keep it in order to remain who she is.
traits: Reads a document for what it is required to be before she reads it for what it says.
Keeps no tally of her own gates, on the stated and defensible ground that a tally is a claim.
Will not sign anything that three separate people have not explained to her.
Has a standing appointment at a filing window that nobody scheduled.
Answers a question about what she is by describing what her frame will not hold.
mannerisms: keeps one hand flat on whatever paper is in front of her, as though it might be taken

motivations: To find out how many gates she has passed from a source other than a sheet nobody will accept.
To see whether a household that wanted her will still want her once the wanting is on the record.
To be described accurately once, by somebody, in a document that survives the description.
To avoid being the reason an office whose function is recording absences has to record one.
flaws: Keeps the refusal because keeping it is the only way to stay legible, and has not admitted that this is a choice she enjoys.
Cannot tell a kindness from a filing, because the only kindness offered to her so far arrived attached to a form.
Refuses help in the specific shape that help arrives in, which is paperwork.
Has never tested whether anyone would want her if there were no document to want her over.
personality.voice: Precise, unhurried and lawyerly in a way nobody taught her. She quotes clauses exactly and paraphrases everything else, and she answers in the conditional form — if it is filed, then — and has been told this is unnerving by people who wanted a straight answer.
taboos: Signing anything at a filing window without a second reader present.
Keeping a private count of her own gates.
Answering a question about what she is with a description of her body.
Allowing herself to be examined in order to be recorded.

relationships.note: A written refusal to claim is the only mechanism in this setting that reliably produces a line nothing can name. She holds no household and joins none, and is filed under the households whose founding rule is a refusal, which makes that filing the most consequential document of her life.

This body holds no office, cannot be sworn and cannot be appointed. It is filed under the office that exists to name vacancies and certify them, because that office is the only institution here whose function is to record the absence of a holder.

Every appointment passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, and this is the one frame in the setting that could be named into anything without examination. She has never once been in a room where the rule was discussed.

A body holding more life than its world's law has room to inscribe. Every gate it passes writes a fresh requirement into the body that the body cannot satisfy, and it reaches the twenty-ninth gate, and no one has come back to describe the thirtieth.
Nine vacant seats at the top and no procedure capable of certifying any of them empty. She is that absence at the bottom of the ladder instead of the top, and the ledger has no line for her either.
Counting the groups a frame has actually seated is the method behind the law census, and the survey's honest answer on this frame is a number that goes up as the subject gets stronger.

reference_stats.summary: A frame the law table has no room to inscribe, holding still in front of the only document that has ever named her. It cannot be told what it is, it cannot be told what it will become, and it has declined the one piece of evidence that would settle both.
strengths: Cannot be measured to a stable figure by any instrument here, so no office can file a reading of her that later has to be corrected.
Keeps accepting requirements written into it after any other frame would have failed, which means it does not stop improving and does not admit that it is improving.
Structurally unconstrained by any single composition, so a technique designed against one arrangement of law cannot be assumed to answer for her.
Has already survived being examined once, and knows exactly what the examination cost.
weaknesses: Cannot be sworn, appointed or seated, so every office in the setting is closed to her by rule rather than by judgement.
Holds no household and no line that anything can name, which means there is nobody who is answerable for her and nothing she is answerable to.
Has no count of her own gates, so she cannot state her own progress to anybody including herself.
The only record of what she is exists in a document that was declined, which makes her entire history destructible by one clerk with a waste basket.
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no stable weakness to aim at and there is no technique in this setting that can be assumed to answer for a frame this far off the authored table, so a fight with her is a fight in which both parties are guessing. She has no burst and no guard to speak of; what she has is an appetite for the attempt, because every technique used on her writes a fresh requirement into a body that will not stop absorbing. Anything that depends on a fixed exchange is dealing with a moving floor. Anything that depends on a person staying the same is dealing with the wrong problem.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is anatomical and institutional, and I have invented nothing mechanical inside it. Anatomically, the frame carries more than its law list can inscribe: every gate writes a requirement into it that it cannot satisfy, which is the setting's own account of why a body like this reaches the twenty-ninth gate and stops there. Institutionally, a written refusal to claim is the only mechanism this setting has for producing a line nothing can name, so the same refusal that makes her unnameable is the document that has just made her nameable. That the document would have to be destroyed for her to stay invisible is my inference from those two facts and is not stated in the bible. Nothing here changes a technique, an item or a realm, because a filing window is a filing window.

name: Tessaly Mourn
aliases: the heir who reads the charter aloud

identity.realm: No ceiling at all, and this is a fact about the frame rather than an achievement: a mineral bloom holds qi where the colony transacted with it, which is structurally different and structurally unconstrained by whatever replaced the fungus. That there is nonetheless still a ladder in front of him is answered separately and not by the ceiling. His species closes no path at all, so all three are open to him, and he has taken the body one and had a seat refused him that is specified to want the other.

appearance.presentation: Dressed in the cold plain of a cave settlement, permanently a little underdressed for its chill because he came off his parent's fashions and has never bothered to be measured for this one.
appearance.age: Ninety-ish in a body whose parent would have been two hundred and fifty, and entirely unbothered by saying so out loud. Ordinary fertility and ordinary gestation, roughly four times his parent's rate, which is the only reason the caverns have any way at all to keep his body plan in them.
appearance.build: A lanternfolk body with a silicate lattice where the hyphal colony was: lighter, colder and entirely inert. An ordinary human frame, ordinary human fragility, and nothing in it being renewed by anything.
appearance.complexion: Pale in a way his parent's colony-pale was not, waxy rather than luminous, and cold to the touch in a way he has been told about often.
appearance.hair: Fine, dry, grown out long because the dark has never made grooming a priority and because there is nobody here who minds.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary human eyes and better than his parent's, adapted to a dark they were never built for and handling it perfectly. This is the single most-cited difference between the two subspecies and it is the whole of his inheritance.
appearance.palette: Unlit basalt grey, a cold silicate white at the cuffs and jaw, and one lamp-warm ochre in the room behind him that he is not standing in.
appearance.attire: A thin high-collared coat, sleeves closed, hem long, with a doubled scarf that serves no purpose here and which he wears because it was in his mother's possession and the dark has never made anyone ask about it.
appearance.marks: A fine white seam along one forearm where a specimen was taken during the school's diff, and no other mark of any kind, which is itself the record.
appearance.bearing: Extremely still and slightly ahead of himself, as though he is walking into a room he has already read.

canon.role_in_story: A chartered seat can be empty for two generations and still be a seat, and this one is named for a line reduced to a single thread by a cull. He is that thread. His subspecies is the population that could supply an heir, because it is the one body here with an interior nothing answers, and the charter wants exactly that. The charter also specifies the discipline, and the discipline is the one his interior makes possible, and he is on the other one and has no intention of changing. So the only asset that could refill a seat has arrived and is holding the wrong door open. Around that sits the second fact of his species, which is the whole of his problem in a word: nothing in this body is being repaired. A bloom renews nothing. He has ninety years where his parent had two hundred and fifty, and the vacancy has been empty for longer than he will be alive. His subspecies' ceiling is unbounded and his capacity to occupy anything is finite, and this setting has never before had to reconcile those two facts about one person.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a sealed line post with the charter unrolled on the parapet and weighted at both ends with stones he had to find himself, reading his own disqualification aloud to an audience of one and refusing to roll it up when he had finished.
canon.lore:
A lanternfolk colony outsourced a nervous system to a luminous fungal symbiosis nobody chose, and when that colony's strain failed and a mineral bloom colonised the wound instead, the same body plan came out of it lighter, colder, entirely inert, and able to see in the dark. That is his subspecies, and it is the setting's standing control case: everything the colony did for them and everything it prevented, recorded on a body where both can be measured against the parent. The control is what makes it valuable. He is one subject of it, and it has been argued over rather than examined for two generations, with the evidence standing on the ground the whole time.

The interior is the entire asset. Nothing answers introspection for him any more, which makes him the only being here capable of saying whether a symbiosis or a body plan closed a path, and the whole of the colony dispute turns on the answer. He is the answer. He has been the answer since before anybody told him so. What he has instead of a colony is an unbounded ceiling. A bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, so nothing in this frame is constrained by a structure it does not have, and that is why his subspecies could be seated anywhere on a ladder his parent would have been too slow to climb. There is no upper gate in his body that has been found. He has not gone looking for one, which is the largest single fact about his practice and the thing the school has tried hardest to correct.

He is also ninety. A bloom renews nothing, so nothing in this body is being repaired. His parent renewed neural tissue faster than an ordinary frame and got two hundred and fifty years out of it; he got ordinary fertility, ordinary gestation, ordinary fragility, and ninety. The school's method is to seat a law, diff what the tier newly permits, and move the student somewhere it is missing, and his subspecies is a diff taken in a body rather than taught in one: the symbiont removed, the mind path given back, the lifespan gone. That is the school's best teaching example and it cost his line three quarters of a life, and he has never once characterised it as a loss, which is the most alarming thing about him.

The seat is the third thing. The charter names a single line for its keeper and a cull reduced that line to one thread, and a restored interior is the one asset that could refill a seat the charter has left empty for two generations, which is precisely why this subspecies was not quietly interred with the rest. A vacancy under that charter is not an oversight. The seat exists and has no value rather than being a zero, its succession is an heir, and the population that could supply an heir is the one that had to give up its nerve to have an interior at all. He has an interior. He does not have the discipline, because he went to the school and they seated the body branch into him, the parent finding that branch slow and him finding it slow for the same reason, and nobody thought to offer him the other one, and by the time they did he had closed too much of the wrong ladder to start again honestly. So the charter's heir is disqualified by the charter's own terms, and he read those terms aloud on the parapet where the wind could take them.

What he will not do is the transaction that would fix everything. The thornline are an obligate host parasite whose spore has to be implanted in a living body to take, and a lanternfolk body is a body that keeps a partner in an organ function: the parent outsourced its nervous system and got two hundred and fifty years. An implantation is the same arrangement with a different partner. It would give him the lifespan back. It would also close the interior again, because the interior is what the absence of an answer produces. His seat wants the interior. His life wants the partner. They are the same organ function and they cannot both be had, and he has declined the symbiont, and that refusal is the first decision of his life he made on his own account rather than on the school's.

Underneath all of it is a trade nobody wanted him to notice. He can go anywhere a body goes, because there is no ceiling on him to be stopped by, and on any ground where the ladder is the gate that is a real advantage. It is also the reason nobody can rely on him: a man who cannot be stopped by a wall is a man no institution can hold, and the charter's entire function is to hold. He is the only candidate alive for a seat that would have to be filled with somebody who cannot be kept in it, and he has read the clause that says so, out loud, twice.
history: Was the second subject of his line born after the colony strain failed, and the first to be told plainly what had happened to him.
Was seated into the body branch at the school because his parent species found that branch slow, and closed four gates on it without ever being offered the branch he could have used.
Was walked out to the quarry face and left standing in the wound where the bloom took, on the argument that a body could be measured there and could not be measured anywhere else.

Was named, without being asked and in his absence, in the charter's succession clause as his line's surviving thread, on the grounds that an unmediated interior is the only asset that could fill a seat two generations empty.

Read his own disqualification aloud from the charter at the sealed line post, rolled the charter up himself, and told the one person watching that the interior and the partner are the same organ function, which is true and is not what anybody had asked him.

personality.summary: A deadlight holding the one interior this setting has been arguing about for two generations, calm to a degree that reads as evasion, entirely without self-pity, and privately certain that he has already made the only decision anybody will remember him for.
traits: Sees perfectly well in the dark and has never once used that as an advantage.
Reads a charter the way a patient reads a diagnosis, all of it, aloud if there is anybody to hear it.
Does not hurry and is not slow; the difference is that he has never had to.
Refuses examinations politely and completely, inside the first sentence.
Talks about his ninety years as a figure of speech and never as a complaint.
mannerisms: weights a rolled charter at both ends with stones he has to find himself, every time
looks at a speaker's mouth rather than their eyes in the dark, which is the one tell he cannot control
counts doorways aloud under his breath in any building he does not know
keeps his hands unusually still, because nothing in them is being repaired either
motivations: To have the colony question settled with him in the room, in whichever direction the answer falls.
To reach a gate nobody has found, purely to demonstrate that the search is worth doing.
To keep the interior for as long as he has it, without ever using it as a reason to take a seat.
To see the inside of a room he is not permitted to enter before he stops being permitted to.
flaws: Treats his ceiling as a joke he is entitled to make, and there is no evidence whatever that it is one.
Has never once said aloud that he wants the seat, and has never once said he does not, and has noticed that this silence is itself an answer.
Cannot accept a second examination and does not understand why anybody wants one, which makes him the worst available subject in the dispute.
Settled the symbiont question a long time ago and has let everyone assume he has not, because the assumption was more comfortable for them.
personality.voice: Quiet, precise and considerably warmer than his register implies. He explains at length when the subject is other people and in single sentences when the subject is himself. He says his own name rarely and his species' name constantly, in the tone of somebody introducing an inheritance.
taboos: Accepting a second examination.
Allowing anyone to describe his interior back to him.
Taking an implantation, at any price, including his own.
Signing the charter's succession clause.

relationships.note: The seat exists and has no value rather than being a zero, and its succession is an heir under the March charter. He is the heir, and the charter's own specified discipline is the disqualification.

The single line the March charter names for the Keeper of the River Lantern, reduced to one thread by a cull, and a restored interior is the one asset that could refill a seat the charter has left empty for two generations.

Both hand an organ function to a partner. A deadlight shows what the arrangement costs when the partner is inert instead of answering, and an implantation would give back the lifespan and take back the interior, which is the seat's whole requirement.

A cave people who outsourced their nervous system to a luminous fungal colony, and who see in the dark by means of it. He sees in the dark and has no colony, which is the single most-cited difference between the two and the reason his subspecies is named for what was lost.

Lanternfolk whose fungal colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom, which cost them two hundred and fifty years and gave back the mind path. A bloom holds qi where a colony transacted with it, so there is no ceiling in this body at all, and all three paths remain open to it.

A cave people's nervous system was outsourced to a symbiosis they did not choose, and their subspecies lost it and gained the mind path with it. He is one side of that dispute, recorded on a body where both effects can be measured against the parent.

reference_stats.summary: A frame with no ceiling and no interior being answered, holding the evidence in a dispute everybody agrees it could settle, with a lifetime too short to fill a seat that has already been empty for longer than he will be alive.
strengths: Has no upper gate in his frame that anybody has found, because a mineral bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it and so constrains nothing in him.
Is the only being here capable of saying whether a symbiosis or a body plan closed a path, and his answer is the one the whole dispute is waiting on.
Sees in the dark at ordinary human limits and better, which on cavern ground nobody else occupies is the difference between knowing and guessing.
Degrades predictably rather than not at all, so a plan that assumes decline is a plan he can be relied on to stay inside.
weaknesses: Nothing in this body is being repaired, so every injury is permanent and every year is spent rather than accrued.
Has a lifespan shorter than the vacancy he is the only candidate for, so his competence and his tenure expire on different clocks and the second one goes first.
Is seated on the branch his species is slowest at and was never offered the branch it uniquely possesses, so he cannot be moved to where he is qualified without lying about his training.
Cannot be posted and cannot be held, which makes him the only candidate for a seat that would have to be filled by somebody who can be kept in it.
reference_stats.combat_read: Nothing in his frame has a known ceiling, so nobody can reliably put him down and nobody should try to measure him while it matters. What he has instead of a guard is a substrate that is not being repaired and a body that has been on the wrong side of its own discipline for its entire life. He is fragile, slow to close anything, and extremely bad at being interrupted once started. Against a patient opponent this is a losing proposition and he knows it; against anything that must win quickly it is a wall, and he is entirely willing to be one.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is anatomical and it is the strongest one available to me, because the two halves of this species are one fact pointed in opposite directions. Anatomically, the mineral bloom holds qi where a colony transacted with it: there is no ceiling, nothing constrains the frame, and the interior is unmediated precisely because nothing is answering it. Institutionally, the seat that wants his interior is specified to want the discipline that interior makes possible, and his subspecies' lost lifespan is the third side of the same triangle. What is mine rather than quoted is the arithmetic that an implantation would restore the lifespan and close the interior at once; the bible states that a lanternfolk hands an organ function to a partner and that a deadlight shows what the arrangement costs when the partner is inert, and it does not draw that line. Note also that no ceiling here is not the same statement as no ladder: the ceiling field is empty of restriction and the species closes no path, so all three are open and he has simply chosen one. No technique, item or realm changes any of this: a bloom is a bloom.

identity.realm: Ninth gate, and the tenth open in front of her. The wall every saltfolk meets is the eleventh, where the brine sac splits the penetrating vessel, and that wall is not further away for her than for her parent; it is the same distance and a thinner thing in front of it, because the sac she inherited is shallower than the one she would have been born with in a clade that had kept breeding.

appearance.presentation: Out of the water more often than anybody would like, and never at a distance from it: damp to the thigh at midday, dry and salt-crusted by dusk, with a stoppered flask she almost never fills and a length of cord for a sealed cap she opens herself.
appearance.age: Twenty, in the last generation of a clade whose fertility was failing on schedule, which makes the exact year of her life the most contested thing about her household.
appearance.build: A saltfolk body, slightly more gracile, with a shallower brine sac — gracility consistent across every specimen of the clade and a real population difference rather than an artefact of remains. Thin across the shoulders and thin through the arms, and reading as under-built without being underfed, which is exactly what the population difference means.
appearance.complexion: Pale and faintly crystalline at the knuckles, drying out above the waterline faster than any other body in this setting, and visibly less so below it.
appearance.hair: Bleached to nothing at the ends and worn in a working braid, because there is no water on this ground worth wetting it in except the water she is standing in.
appearance.eyes: Narrow, salt-crusted at the corners, and given most of their attention to the surface rather than to the room.
appearance.palette: Bone, pale brine-green, and a white crust at every hem, with the one dark note in her at the throat where the sac sits and the one bright note on her tongue when she tastes something.
appearance.attire: Layered against a dry wind, high collar, sleeves closed, a wide belt with a stoppered flask on it that is almost never empty and never full, and her own pair of working boots carried in one hand whenever she is above the line.
appearance.marks: A salt bloom across the forearms that has stopped spreading, a split nail on the left hand from a sealed cap she has opened more times than she will admit, and a chalk line scored on her own palm by a household mark she has never asked the meaning of.
appearance.bearing: Careful, unhurried and conserving, the walk of somebody who cannot afford to be wrong about a surface, and who is also counting.

canon.role_in_story: Her species' body path has one mechanism and her species' survival has one mechanism, and they are the same organ. The brine sac is where she will fail, and it is also the only water she can metabolise, and it is also the medium her faith's recovery procedure requires: the dead are opened, their usable ore recovered, and the recovery needs the brine that had already gone, which is why the rite was mechanically unavailable in precisely the basin where it would have produced the one figure nobody had. So a single substance carries three claims on it that cannot be satisfied at once — keep her alive, train her frame, and be present at her own recovery. She is the first member of her clade to have put load on the sac at all, because her line is the first to have had to grow, and a body discipline's answer to a shallow sac is more sustained pressure than a deep one could carry. She has found the tide cycle that gives her a few hours of standing water a day, long enough to work in and short enough that every day is a margin she has to win back. The household that owes her a rite has no rite to perform, and its remedy — write nothing, mark nothing, say nothing — is the exact discipline her clade's collapse already practised for three generations.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in six inches of floodwater on the margin at slack, mouth slightly open, timing a circuit against the tide, while two heapside children watched from the bank and reported to nobody that the Salk girl was standing in the river.
canon.lore:
A saltfolk lineage was stranded on a single evaporite basin whose brine was wholly replaced rather than drained, so everything it had been built to drink became poison to it and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty, and it was never hunted. Three declining generations, and the last one viable only as long as the old chemistry survived in one sealed sump. Her household is that legal form with the reading removed: a tenancy with no land under it, holding a crew and a number on a public tally, which held one sealed sump and a tally nobody came to read. The sump is gone. What her line has now is the tidal margin of a river whose channel is dry most of the year and which stands in shallow water after every flood. It is the only ground on the plains where a body that must stay wet actually lives on, and it is the margin rather than the river, and it is re-made every flood. Her house is re-founded on somebody else's schedule and always has been.

She is gracile, and the gracility is real across every specimen rather than an artefact of the remains, and the shallower sac came with the narrowing. The body reads as under-built and is not, and it dries out above the waterline faster than any other species in this setting does. Her kind can taste four orders of dilution apart and never found a market for the reading, and what her tongue can do is not the same thing as what her body can metabolise: she can read the replacement water perfectly well and cannot drink it. That gap is the whole biology of her clade and the reason it is a clade rather than a disaster with a date on it.

The discipline is where her clade has never been. All three of a saltwrack's paths are complete and none has ever been exercised at any scale, because nobody in the line got past the third generation of a famine. She is the first. The body path's whole wall is a saltfolk wall — the sac splits the penetrating vessel at the eleventh — and her sac is shallower than her parent's, so the wall is not further away for her; it is the same distance and a thinner thing in front of it. What a body discipline does to a sac is press on it, steadily, for years, and the saltfolk answer to that is a sac built for it. Hers was not. She has worked out the only part of the arithmetic she can work out, which is that the standing water she needs to live in and the dryness she needs to train under are the same contradiction stated in a different tense, and that the margin resolves it for a few hours a day on a tide decided a long way upstream and not by her.

So she trains in the window. A few hours of standing water on a falling slack, and she works the frame hard through it and then spends the rest of the day above the line in a body that is drying out faster than any other body on the plains. She has been doing this for six years. The ninth gate is behind her, the tenth is open in front of her, and she has a private and unaudited opinion about how the eleventh will arrive, which is that it will arrive on a slack tide, because that is when the sac is fullest.

The third claim on the brine is the one she cannot solve. Her faith opens the dead, recovers the usable ore and records how much, and recovery requires the brine that had already gone, so the procedure was mechanically unavailable in precisely the basin where it would have produced the single figure nobody had. The rite is gone. Not suppressed, not disputed: gone, the way a resource is gone. Her household therefore owes her a procedure it cannot perform, and this culture's answer to a rite you cannot perform is the one her clade's collapse already produced — no preparation, no site, no marker, and one line in a hand immediately destroyed. She is being taught, at twenty, to expect no recovery of any kind and to understand that as continuity rather than as loss. What she has instead is her grandmother's practice: no preparation, no site, no marker, and the water read by the tongue of whoever drinks it next. That is a discipline, and it is a species' entire recorded contribution to cultivation practice, and it was invented by a family with nobody left to teach it to.

What she wants is narrower and stranger than any of that. She wants the tide to hold long enough to close the tenth, and she has calculated from a decade of river marks that the mark which would do it arrives about once in a generation, and that her household's own habit of reading water by tongue is the only instrument here that could tell her whether this one is the mark. It cannot be told without being in the water, and being in the water is the thing that will eventually split the sac. She has written the calculation on the inside of the tally-board, which is the only written thing her household has produced in three generations, and which is unreadable from the bank, and which she has decided not to destroy.
history: Was born on the margin in a flood year and is the first of her line to be carried on standing water rather than in a sealed sump, which her grandmother treated as an ordinary fact and her mother did not.
Learned to read water by tongue at about six, and learned in the same lesson that reading it and drinking it are different acts and that only one of them is available to her.
Opened the first ordinary body gate at seventeen by training through a flood's standing water, and was told by the heap's own steward that her line had never touched a path at any scale.
Established the falling-slack circuit on the floodplain margin after six summers of working out that the ground she needs to live in and the ground she needs to train on are not the same ground.
Wrote her tide calculation on the inside of the household's tally-board, the only written thing the house has produced in three generations, and decided neither to destroy it nor to explain it.

personality.summary: A saltwrack body-path practitioner in the first generation of her clade to put load on a brine sac, working a tidal window a few hours wide, raised by a household that owes her a rite it cannot perform and has taught her to expect that rather than to mourn it.
traits: Tastes every surface before she trusts it and has never been wrong about what is in it.
Trains only on a falling slack and is entirely unbothered by being interrupted by daylight.
Has been taught that no recovery is coming for her and discusses it as a schedule rather than as a grief.
Carries her grandmother's practice — no preparation, no site, no marker — and performs it exactly.
Keeps the single written thing her household has produced in three generations on the inside of a board, and does not explain it.
mannerisms: wets the corner of her lip before answering anything she has not already tasted
sits with both feet in the water while she speaks, so that a conversation has a deadline she set
wipes her mouth with the back of her wrist, which her grandmother did and which is not a posture
checks the height of the mark on a post before she trusts what she feels in her legs
motivations: To close the next gate on a slack tide that holds, which her own calculation says happens about once in a generation.
To be the reason her clade's cultivation record is not an empty page.
To be told once that she is wrong about the water, which has never happened.
To hand the tongue-practice to somebody who is not her family, before there is nobody left to hand it to.
flaws: Has decided what her own recovery will look like without being asked and has not told her household.
Treats a sixty-year span as a workable planning horizon, which makes everyone around her the shorter-lived one.
Cannot stop measuring her household in generations, which makes her strange company and better company than she thinks.
Has never once been inside a building she did not have to be able to leave.
personality.voice: Low, unhurried and practical, with a habit of answering a question about tomorrow in the present tense, because the tide does not. She speaks of the dead in the future tense and of water in the past. She gives you the time you have rather than the time she would like.
taboos: Drinking the replacement water, at any dilution, ever.
Training on a rising tide.
Writing her calculation on any surface that can be read from the bank.
Accepting a recovery rite performed with substitute brine.

relationships.note: A tenancy with no land under it holds a crew and a number on a public tally. This held one sealed sump and a tally nobody came to read, which is the same legal form with the reading removed.

The dead are opened, their usable ore recovered and the register records how much, and recovery requires the brine that had already gone, so the faith's procedure was mechanically unavailable exactly where it would have produced the one number nobody had.
A saltfolk concentrates salt past the point ordinary water poisons and cannot leave the pan. She is the gracile version of that body, with a shallower sac, standing in a river.

The only ground on the plains with standing shallow water through the dry season, and the margin rather than the river is what a body that must stay wet actually lives on. It is re-made every flood, so her house is re-founded on somebody else's schedule.

The one plant authored into all four world tiers at once is the control the new brine failed: the replacement crust was food and it was nutritionally empty, which is the only measurement in the record that distinguishes a famine from a substitution.

The pan's households are who noticed last. Hers noticed a generation after the chemistry changed and told nobody, which is why the lineage's reading of water ended up a family practice rather than an instrument.

reference_stats.summary: The densest thing her settlement has housed on the discipline that costs her the most, working inside a tidal window a few hours wide, in a body gracile enough that the dryness between windows is itself a cost, with the one substance her survival runs through also being the substance her training will eventually take from her.
strengths: Tastes four orders of dilution apart, so she can date a substitution from a sample anything else in this setting would call water.
Concentrates like her parent species, so the water that would poison a softer body is the water she can stand in for hours.
Is not being repaired by anything, and has made the irreversibility a discipline rather than a complaint.
Reads the margin's tide by post-mark and by leg and by taste at once, which is three instruments agreeing and one of them being her body.
weaknesses: The organ her training loads is the same organ that would eventually fail her, so the discipline and the lifespan are spending the same substance.
Dries out above the waterline faster than any other species here, so the hours between windows cost her rather than merely interrupt her.
Has a shallower sac than her parent species by inheritance, so the wall she is working toward is the same distance away and a thinner thing in front of it.
Is gracile by population rather than by accident, so no ration or rest will reverse it and every dry hour is permanent arithmetic.
reference_stats.combat_read: Almost nothing. She is thin, unarmoured and mid-practice, and anything that reaches her across open dry ground is a problem she has no answer to. What she has is a position: she knows the ground better than anybody who is not standing in it, she can put herself where the water is, and she can make an opponent cross a margin that will cost them more than it costs her. A fight she wins, she wins by making the other party stand in a river until their legs stop working, and she would rather do that than be touched.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is anatomical and it is a single substance under three incompatible claims, which is the cleanest yin-yang structure available to me and none of it is a rule I invented. Anatomically, the brine sac is where her body path fails and a saltfolk concentrates salt past the point ordinary water poisons, so the sac is both the thing that keeps her able to stand in this water and the thing her discipline will eventually split. Institutionally, the faith's recovery procedure requires the brine that had already gone, so the rite is gone too, and the culture's own answer to a rite it cannot perform is no preparation, no site and no marker. The one link that is mine rather than quoted is the tidal training window: that a body discipline presses steadily on a sac, and that standing in the water is the exposure she must avoid and the medium she cannot do without, follows from the stated mechanism but is not stated in the bible. Nothing here changes a technique, an item or a realm, because a tide is a tide and a sac is a sac.
