identity.realm: Seventh gate, and the eighth is the ceiling rather than a wall in front of her. The eighth gate completes the ordinary meridian set at the liver, the suspended mineral load in her blood filters through the liver, and the liver is the first organ to fail under it — so she stops one step short of the reservoirs because she cannot hold the last ordinary meridian. This is a chemistry fact and not a failure of will, and she has been able to feel the organ working since her second season.

appearance.presentation: Enrolled in the belt's ordinary grey with the collar turned up and sewn through, so the doubled cloth reads as a uniform to anybody who has not counted the seams. She is the settlement's densest person and its most visible, and wears neither fact as a display.
appearance.age: Young, and young for her species' ceiling, which the belt's measuring practice calls being born at the end of the road. She has been eating a working face since she was old enough to be enrolled and has never once been posted out of it.
appearance.build: Compact, dense and square through the chest, with a chambered nasal sieve and a grinding crop under the jaw that is never empty and never still. The frame is genuinely dense under load and does not fatigue; it tightens instead of depleting.
appearance.complexion: Ash-grey from the knuckles to the elbows where the air sits longest on her, with a darker band at the throat where her own load settles before it settles anywhere else.
appearance.hair: Cropped short and coarse and the colour of settled grit, cut with a grit-shear because an ordinary blade goes dull in her hand inside a week.
appearance.eyes: Narrow, placid, and the least used organ she owns. Everything she knows arrives at the distance of a palm rather than across a room, which is a range the belt teaches and she has never had cause to extend.
appearance.palette: Settled grey, oxide red in the seams of the coat, and the dull sulfur yellow of a stone that has rained on, with one chalk-white mark at the wall post that is the only straight line in her life.
appearance.attire: A full-length house coat, high collar, sleeves doubled to the elbow and sewn through, a second wrap inside the first, and a hip pouch of grit-shear, chalk and a length of binding cord she has never once used on anything that could be untied.
appearance.marks: Grey pitted enamel, which her species takes from grit rather than from diet, and one scored line across the ridge of the crop-bone where a haul harness has taken the load for longer than the harness has existed.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still and slightly downwind. The stillness is a body that cannot turn quickly; the downwind is a habit older than any office she has ever held.

canon.role_in_story: The one reproductive requirement her species has is a spatial one: a pair must be within sight of one another through the ember season or conception does not hold, and that single clause sets the whole social spacing of the belt. Every settlement on the ash-fall ground is therefore laid out around who can see whom for six weeks a year. The belt's settlements have been laid out for a generation against a wall that faces the wrong way, because every holder of that shore built facing arrivals and the outside came indoors and stayed, so the spacing her species needs is being compressed by a geometry nobody living chose. She is on the body path and her frame is the densest thing her settlement has ever housed, and the discipline she practises requires the one thing her body does on its own and cannot choose: sustained particulate load, converted into frame density. She trains by breathing. There is no regimen, no dose and no teacher that can substitute for the air. So the settlement has one belt, the belt is narrowing, and she and a commonborn with a frame that tightens faster than hers have been put in sight of one another through the season because the ground allows it, which is not a decision anybody made and is nevertheless a decision.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the inside face of the settlement wall during the ember season at the one hour when the two sightlines overlap, waiting, with her chin lifted, in a place where the wall is on the wrong side of the thing it was built for.
canon.lore:
A body that breathes volcanic grit and keeps it: a chambered nasal sieve lined with cilia that traps the rock and passes it into a crop for grinding, a thickened dermis, a dark mineral-charged blood, and enamel grey and pitted from grit rather than from diet. Her kind process stone into protein and are the only reason the ash-fall belt has a food chain at all. Smell is effectively gone and is replaced by the sieve's direct contact sense, and they taste minerals the way anyone else tastes salt, which makes them the only population that can tell two ash grades apart by tongue. That is the whole of their inheritance from the ground, and it is why every ration, roster and office on the belt is written against a person whose sieve loads.

They stop at the eighth gate. That gate completes the ordinary meridian set at the liver, and the mineral load in her blood has been filtering through the liver since the year she was born, so the ceiling is a chemistry fact rather than a failure of will. The eighth gate is the one they cannot pass and it is the organ they spend their lives loading. They are closed on the mind path outright, because the same grit occludes the fine capillary beds introspection needs and the species has no faculty left for it. So the body path is not a preference for her kind; it is the entire available surface.

What is interesting about that surface is that it requires nothing. She trains by breathing the belt. Spent ground, storm-thrown ash, the lee side of a spoil face, the floor under a grinding shed: all of it converts. A body discipline that sustains a particulate load turns that load into frame density, and the belt is the only place in this setting where the conversion is free, so the most expensive training regime available to her is also the one she never has to seek out. And that is the trap. Her species cannot be posted, reassigned or dismissed, so the belt is the only home her kind has and off it she declines steadily rather than travelling. Every advantage of the body resolves into the same fact: she has nowhere else to go and nothing to do there.

The second advantage pairs honestly with the first, and it is the one nobody on the belt will use against her. A dense frame cannot be posted out of a settlement, cannot be sent across the wall and cannot be dismissed from a ration, so her presence in any room is permanent and her weight in any argument is structural. The belt has noticed this. It has also noticed that a person who cannot be sent away and cannot be refused is a person whose attendance is a form of policy. A rift is a door with a timetable because it closes when the out-of-range law value returns inside its range, and every holder of that shore built their wall facing arrivals. So the belt's outside has been permanently indoors for a generation, and the ground on the far side of the wall — the ground the wall was built to keep out — is now the belt's own overflow. Nobody rebuilt. The wall is still the correct wall for a threat that used to be outside, and she is standing on its wrong side by assignment.

Her species has exactly one reproductive requirement and it is spatial: a pair must be within sight of one another through the ember season or conception does not hold. That single clause sets the spacing of the whole settlement, and it has always been answerable, because the belt used to be wider than its people. It is narrower now. Two sightlines that overlapped on a wide belt have been forced into the same block by a wall that took the ground it faces, and the settlement responded the way settlements respond, by pairing whoever happened to be on one line of sight. She has been put on the same line as a commonborn with a frame that tightens faster than hers and no ceiling to slow him before she has been asked anything at all, and both of them know what the season is, and neither of them has said that they know.

What she is actually training for is the seventh gate, and the seventh is not hard. The reason she is not further along is that the discipline's only input is the air she is standing in, and she spends the ember season standing in a place where the ash is thin because that is where the sightlines are. She is slower through the season than she is out of it by a margin she has measured, and she has measured it because nobody else in the settlement could.

What she will not do is take a denser intake to make up the difference, and this is the part the settlement finds difficult. Her practice is free because the air is free, and the belt's one rite of entry is the conversion itself: no second rite, no form, no ceremony, only the season you take the ground into your body and what it does to you afterwards. So the discipline that makes her the densest thing in the settlement is also the discipline that decides whether anybody can live in the settlement, and a settlement trying to work out how many of its people it can hold on the far side of a wall it built facing the wrong way has no procedure for the question. She has noticed that she is the answer to it and has not said so, because the answer is a figure and figures about her own frame are the one thing her species has never had a market for.
history: Was enrolled at the conversion into a working face at the age the belt considers early, on the strength of a palate that could separate two falls of ash the eye had already agreed were the same.
Closed the sixth gate at fourteen and the seventh at sixteen, both faster than any enrolled body trained beside her, and both slower than she has since measured herself to be through an ember season.
Was moved to the inside face of the settlement wall for the sightline without being consulted, in the season her household could least afford to lose a working pair.
Worked out that the two sightlines from the inside wall and the far ground overlap for about an hour, and that this is the whole of her margin, and began timing it.
Declined, once and out loud, to raise her intake to make up the ember-season deficit, in front of the people who had offered the dirt, and has been called difficult by three of them since.

personality.summary: An ashwalker body-path practitioner whose training regimen is free, whose ceiling is an organ she loads daily, and whose species' one reproductive requirement has been compressed into an hour of sightline by a wall that faces the wrong way.
traits: Grades ash by tongue at the distance of a palm and is the only person in the settlement who can.
Trains by breathing, and has never once had to seek out a regimen.
Times her sightline off a post mark and has never told anyone what she is timing.
Cannot be posted, reassigned or dismissed, and has never had to insist on any of it.
Declines a denser intake to the face, in front of people who meant it kindly.
mannerisms: turns downwind before answering anything, so the answer is given out of clean air
sits with her back to a wall and her face to the sightline at once, which is uncomfortable and is deliberate
grinds her thumb along the pitting in her own enamel when a conversation turns to what she ought to have done
keeps her chin lifted and her eyes still while listening, which on her species is the whole performance of attention
motivations: To close the next gate on her own intake rather than on dirt somebody else provided.
To be asked what she is timing, and to have to give a real answer.
To widen the overlap by an hour without anybody rebuilding the wall.
To be somewhere on this belt in twenty years, which for her kind is the entire ask.
flaws: Has a built ceiling she has accepted as fact, and so has never checked whether the gate before it was her limit.
Has not told anyone that the sightline is a pairing, and prefers the ambiguity to having it named.
Cannot accept a favour that arrives with dirt in it, which makes most of what the belt offers her unusable.
Is the densest thing in the settlement and treats that as a property rather than as a responsibility.
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried and given almost entirely in grades and distances. She states an intake and stops. She has no idiom for her own ceiling and describes it the way she would describe a shift pattern, and when somebody tries to give her a feeling about it she changes the subject to the air.
taboos: Taking an intake from spoil or leavings that was offered as a gift.
Naming the sightline out loud in front of the settlement.
Accepting a posting off the belt, on any ground.
Answering a question about her own frame with a figure she has not tasted for herself.

relationships.note: A body that breathes volcanic grit and keeps it: a chambered nasal sieve that traps the rock and passes it into a crop for grinding, a thickened dermis, a dark mineral-charged blood, and enamel pitted from grit rather than from diet.

A rift is a door with a timetable because it closes when the out-of-range law value returns inside its range, and every holder of that shore built their wall facing arrivals, so the belt's outside has been permanently indoors for a generation. This is what breathes the difference.
Reed is burned to clear marsh for grazing. The ashwalkers need the belt and the marshfolk need the reed, and neither of them can move, and both of them are right about their own evidence.

The grey lichen colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, so every cut and every trial on this belt leaves a map, and a body that absorbs residual qi straight out of ash and stone follows that map without ever having been taught to.
Both solve the same problem of living in hot grit from opposite ends: the emberblood runs hot, the ashwalker runs cool and filters. The belt has both and the two have no shared practice of any kind.

Nobody on the plains expects to ascend and the work is judged by what survives the season. The belt's commons is the one population whose survival is measured in kilograms of air rather than in harvests, and whose presence on the ground is itself the cost of cutting the face.

reference_stats.summary: The densest thing her settlement houses, on a discipline whose entire input is the air she is already standing in, stopped at a gate her own practice has been loading since birth, and standing exactly where a wall's geometry has put her.
strengths: Converts sustained particulate load into frame density, so on the belt her growth is a function of the belt's waste rather than of anybody's budget.
Cannot be posted, reassigned or dismissed, so every plan that assumes she might leave is a plan with no alternative branch.
Grades two falls of ash apart by tongue at the distance of a palm, which is the only sensory range that matters on ground where visibility is measured in minutes.
Absorbs residual qi straight out of ash and worked stone, so she follows every cut on the belt without ever having been taught to.
weaknesses: Stops at the eighth gate because the organ that fails her first is the organ her practice loads, and she has known that since her second season.
Loses an exchange the moment it moves past the distance of a palm, so every argument she wins is won at close range or not at all.
Cannot leave the belt at all, and declines steadily off it, which turns every plan that assumes she might go into a plan with no branch.
Is the settlement's densest body and its single largest particulate load, which makes her a standing answer to a question the settlement has no procedure for asking.
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no burst in her and no retreat in her, only a body getting denser while it stands there, and a person who has watched a dense frame absorb a working day loses interest in interrupting one. The one thing that beats her is anything that keeps its distance, because she reads at the distance of a palm and everything she has ever fought came to her. Off the belt she has no answer at all. Nobody can post her anywhere, so a fight she is moved out of is a fight she does not get to have, and the fact that she cannot be reassigned is a real strength and a real trap and it is the same fact.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is anatomical and institutional, and both halves are the setting's rather than mine. Anatomically, the species breathes grit and keeps it: the suspended mineral load settles on the liver first, the liver is the last ordinary vessel, and the same grit occludes the fine vessels introspection needs, which is why the mind path is closed outright and the eighth gate is the ceiling. Institutionally, the belt's own rites treat the conversion as the whole of enrolment — there is no second rite, no form, no ceremony, only the season you take the ground into your body — so the densest person in a settlement is also the person whose presence determines whether the settlement can be breathed in. What is mine rather than quoted is the compression of the sightline: the species' stated requirement is that a pair hold sight of one another through the ember season, and the wall is stated to face the wrong way; the arithmetic joining them is mine. No technique, item or realm changes any of it, because an intake is an intake.
